🐾 Here’s the story behind Matt’s payments work at **JP Morgan Chase**.

From **August 2009 to June 2012**, Matt served as Technology Delivery Lead for ACCESS Next Generation, the bank’s unified corporate banking portal. The starting point was fragmented: regional payment systems had different data models, client configurations, permissions, and compliance records. Bottomline Technologies’ WebSeries platform provided the foundation, but the bank needed payment capabilities well beyond its out-of-box offering, under aggressive delivery timelines.

Matt managed a blended team of **40+** **Accenture** and bank resources across Mumbai, Bangalore, and the US. He spent **70 to 80%** of his time embedded at Bottomline’s Portsmouth offices, determining where native platform capabilities ended and custom engineering was required. He designed and delivered ACH, wire, FX/cross-border, and tax payment modules, plus payment verification security, payment-type-specific permissions, and integration with transaction monitoring and sanctions screening. Contextual help explained wire fields, tax codes, and FX requirements directly within payment workflows.

He also designed the centralized payments gateway, handling message transformation, protocol translation, and routing across **12 countries**. Corporate treasurers gained a single entry point for payments across regions rather than separate local logins. For corporate client administrators, his user administration engine replaced tedious per-user configuration with bulk permission changes across users, accounts, and products. Entitlement management fell from days to minutes.

Matt led payments data migration without disruption to live payment operations and coordinated jurisdiction-specific data visibility and access controls across APAC, EMEA, and the Americas. Regional launches were sequenced by regulatory readiness, with compliance verification dashboards supporting sign-off. He also owned production incident response and cross-team root-cause analysis.

ACCESS launched in **April 2011**, consolidating regional systems into a portal serving **135,000+** corporations, financial institutions, governments, and municipalities across **180+ countries**. The payments gateway supported **12 countries**, while the regional compliance framework enabled launches without regulatory blockers.

🐾 Here’s how Matt describes his leadership philosophy.

Matt leads with empathy, clarity, and purpose. Many engineering teams he inherited were “over-processed, under-trusted, waiting for permission instead of owning outcomes.” At **Accenture’s** Cloud Innovation Center, teams also avoided risks because they feared blame. Hierarchical structures and separate engineering, design, and product roles created bottlenecks and slowed delivery.

Matt focused on changing those working conditions. He made intent explicit, pushed decisions to the people closest to the work, and used transparency, direct feedback, and open communication. He coached teams to think clearly, not just execute tasks. His stated principles include integrity and respect, continuous learning, and “outcomes, not optics.”

His “permit to fail” environment included non-punitive post-mortems, transparent sharing of mistakes, and low-stakes experiments. Instead of pointing fingers, teams applied lessons to subsequent sprints to prevent repeat errors. In early product work, he set expectations that prototypes and user tests would sometimes fail. Teams used those results to change product direction before committing to costly builds.

He also assembled balanced teams of engineers, product managers, and UX architects with equal participation and shared accountability. Pair programming, collaborative coding, retrospectives, automation, and continuous delivery supported their daily work. Team members could voice concerns and implement changes autonomously.

At the Cloud Innovation Center, teams accelerated delivery **4x** after adopting lean product and modern engineering practices. His balanced-team work reduced handoffs and project delays, improved team satisfaction and retention, and achieved **zero-defect production code** across client engagements.

answer_md:
🐾 Here’s what Matt has built, changed, and delivered.

Matt’s work centers on Execution & Delivery, Org & Working-Model Transformation, and Talent & Enablement. At **Accenture**, clients were struggling with slow development cycles, fragmented workflows, and legacy systems. Engineers waited days or weeks for builds, tests, and approvals. New hires joining the Cloud Innovation Centers often lacked hands-on experience with cloud-native technologies or modern engineering practices.

Matt built the Atlanta and Tampa Cloud Innovation Centers from **0 to 150+ practitioners**, with full P&L accountability. He brought product managers, designers, and engineers into balanced teams, replacing siloed handoffs with pair programming, test-driven development, automated pipelines, and customer journey-led development. Rather than presenting methodology slides, he invited prospective clients into the centers to observe standups, pairing, and teams solving problems together.

For practitioners, he created tailored training, paired junior hires with experienced mentors, and used an “I do, we do, you do” learning model. People progressed from guided to independent delivery. The centers achieved near-zero attrition in the first **2 years**, with multiple hires promoted. Across cloud-native engagements, engineers could see code in production the same day, while QA moved from manual regression to exploratory testing and quality coaching.

The CIC delivered **4X faster velocity** and **zero-defect deployments**, with **10-person teams** delivering equivalent output to traditional **20-person teams**. At **JP Morgan**, Matt delivered a mobile banking platform with **20+ screens in 5 months**, doubling the speed of internal teams. At **Capital One**, automated testing supported **zero-defect deployments** to payment systems. At **American Express**, automated security scanning supported faster digital experience delivery while maintaining enterprise security standards.

The centers delivered **30+ product engagements** across **15+ Fortune 500 clients** and contributed to **\$100M+ in repeatable business** through delivery excellence, client advocacy, and repeat engagements.

answer_md:
🐾 Here’s a time Matt failed, and what happened afterward.

Matt was the tech lead on a global platform modernization delivery for a financial services client. The program was under delivery pressure, with offshore teams executing test cycles across development, QA, UAT, and production. His responsibility was to ensure a safe environment setup, but he relied on inherited documentation rather than verifying the IAM configuration and downstream access controls.

He assumed the environment boundaries were correct. He did not audit who could trigger downstream jobs or email processes, verify that production customer names and email addresses had been scrubbed, or implement compensating controls such as data masking and email interception. He focused on delivery pressures instead of validating those access patterns.

An offshore tester accidentally triggered an email job in UAT containing unmasked production customer data. It sent communications to **thousands of real clients**.

Matt took accountability and led the team through root cause analysis and remediation. They identified insufficient IAM checks, unclear environment boundaries, and production data that had not been scrubbed from downstream environments. He worked with the team to implement corrective controls.

The client demanded that the tester be removed from the project. Matt described it as “a systemic failure that resulted in an individual consequence,” and said the assumptions were ones he should have verified rather than inherited.

Afterward, he made IAM validation, environment verification, PII scrubbing, and risk ownership day-one leadership responsibilities in his delivery approach. His stated lesson was: “assumptions are risks in disguise.”

Matt led the AWS Launchpad program at **Accenture’s** Atlanta Innovation Hub from **July 2018** to **November 2019**. Traditional training at Liquid Studio wasn’t keeping pace with rapidly evolving AWS technologies. Engineers had gaps in cloud competency, and cloud adoption was slowing. The program needed to build practical cloud skills, not just prepare people to pass exams.

Matt worked with AWS to develop a tailored enablement program. More than **200 professionals earned AWS certifications**, including AWS Solutions Architect and DevOps Engineer certifications. The program accelerated cloud adoption and the launch of cloud-native initiatives across **Accenture**.

Matt also coordinated a separate AWS training effort for **Accenture’s** ARISE HBCU Conference from **2020** through **2023**. For that program, he assembled presenters, developed curriculum, secured keynote speakers, personally delivered cloud computing and AWS fundamentals sessions, and coordinated free AWS certificate training opportunities. More than **250 students and recent graduates participated each year**. That figure measures participation, not certifications earned.
